item.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"Q016_pdb_1acc_domain_split","answer":"SCOP 1.75 treated PDB 1acc chain A too coarsely: the old 1accA domain definition was later split in SCOPe into separate numbered SCOPe domain units, rather than being kept as one evolutionary unit for the whole chain. For 1accA, this means the aconitase chain should be interpreted as a multidomain protein: its Fe-S/core aconitase domains and its C-terminal/swing domain are related at different structural levels and should not be collapsed into one family-level homolog. The change illustrates that a PDB chain, and even an older SCOP domain boundary, is not automatically a single transferable evolutionary module. Homology searches should therefore be run and interpreted domain-by-domain using the newer SCOPe split domains; a hit to only one 1accA domain supports homology only for that module. It is unsafe to transfer full-chain aconitase function, active-site architecture, domain arrangement, or use the whole 1accA chain as a modeling template unless the query covers the corresponding domains with compatible boundaries and architecture.","evidence_used":["pretrained model knowledge"]}]}
